---
title: "The sheet in a window"
description: >-
  Ctrl+Alt+Space opens the contact sheet in a Zotero window of its own: the same on all three systems, with search, keyboard, menus and the handoff to the reader.
---

zotLook has three tiers, and the third is the complete one. **Space** shows
the attachment in the system's preview. **Ctrl+Shift+Space** puts the contact
sheet into that same preview. **Ctrl+Alt+Space** opens the sheet in a Zotero
window of its own — and that is the tier on which everything the sheet can do
works, and works the same everywhere.

Three things set the window apart:

- **It is the same on all three systems.** The system previews are three
  different programs with three different windows; the Zotero window is
  Zotero's own, and the sheet in it behaves not just alike but identically on
  macOS, Linux and Windows.
- **It does everything.** The system previews run no scripts; the window does.
  That is why the search and the keyboard exist only here; the menus, the
  annotations and the handoff to the reader it has anyway.
- **On Linux it is the only way to a clickable sheet.** Sushi's renderer
  cannot follow a `zotero:` link; in the window a click opens the page as it
  does everywhere else.

Space remains the quicker reach for a single attachment, and the sheet in the
system preview remains the glance over a document with no window opening. The
window is for working with the sheet: searching, jumping, walking through a
book with the keyboard, and opening the page.

## Opening and closing

**Ctrl+Alt+Space** on a selected item opens the window with the sheet of the
PDF or, for a book, with its [page
overview](features.qmd#a-page-overview-of-a-book). While it is still empty the
window says that the sheet is on its way; the first time the sheet is built,
after that it comes from the [kept previews](settings.qmd#kept-previews).

The same shortcut closes the window again — so do **Escape**, **Space** and
**q**, the keys that close the system preview. A click on a page hands over
to the reader, which opens at that page, and the window closes behind the
handoff.

The window keeps the size it was dragged to and opens so the next time; the
[window size setting](settings.qmd#the-contact-sheet) shows the value and
takes a typed one too. The shortcut is
[configurable](settings.qmd#shortcuts).

## The menus

A button in each corner: the document's contents, read from the PDF's
outline, and its annotations in reading order with quotation, comment and
page. A click on an entry brings the page to the middle of the window,
framed. An annotation also carries the link **Open in the reader**: it opens
the reader not just at the page but at the annotation itself, selected. Both
exist in the system preview as well; in the window the menus answer the
keyboard too.

## The search

A field in the top corner, also reached with **Ctrl+F**, takes a word or a
phrase: pages without it are dimmed, pages with it show how often, the first
is brought to the middle, and **Enter** walks on to the next. The text comes
off the pages as the sheet is drawn, so a scan without a text layer has
nothing to search. In a book's page overview the hits are marked in the
tiles.

A word standing in Zotero's own search field when the window opens goes
along and is searched first: whoever searched the library for a term sees at
once where it sits in the document.

The system previews have no field, since they run no scripts; the sheet there
is the same, minus the search.

## The keyboard

The frame is a cursor:

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| **Enter** | frames the next page — the first, on the first press — or, with a search, the next hit; **Shift+Enter** goes back |
| **Arrow keys** | move the frame across the grid, a row at a time up and down; with a search, left and right go hit by hit, and up and down to the nearest row above or below that has a hit |
| **o**, or **Ctrl+Enter** | opens the framed page in the reader, as a click does, and the window closes behind it |
| **c** / **a** | open the contents or the annotations; the arrows walk the entries, **Enter** goes to the entry's page, **o** on an annotation opens the reader at it, the same letter closes the menu |
| **digits**, then **Enter** | frame the page of that number; the digits show beside the search field as they are typed |
| **+** / **−** | one column more or fewer, on the spot; the default in the settings stays |
| **p** | prints the sheet — the print dialogue is where it becomes a PDF |
| **Page Up** / **Page Down** | scroll |
| **Space**, **q**, **Escape** | close the window |

In the search field a letter is typing, and the left and right arrows move
the caret; the up and down arrows work there as they do outside it. Enter
walks on to the next hit and hands the keyboard back to the page, so the next
**o** opens rather than types; **Ctrl+F** is the way back into the field.

## Dark where the system is dark

The sheet follows the system's appearance: on a dark desktop the ground, the
menus and the search field turn dark, and the pages stay the paper they are.
That holds in the window and in the system previews alike.

## Without a system preview

Where no system preview answers Space — Sushi not installed, QuickLook not
running — the sheet opens in its window instead. The
[setting](settings.qmd#the-contact-sheet) turns that off; then the press is
logged and nothing shows.

## Several items: the collection sheet

With several items selected, the same shortcut makes a **collection sheet**
of them: a tile per item with the first page of its PDF, and its title, first
creator and year underneath. A click opens the document in the reader, the
keyboard walks the tiles as it walks the pages of a document, and the search
finds an item by title, author or the text of its first page. An item without
a PDF gets an empty tile with its title; a click on it selects the item in
Zotero. It is the look over a collection the forum asked for as a gallery:
select a collection, Ctrl+A, and the shortcut.

The collection sheet is made for the system preview too, with
Ctrl+Shift+Space, without the search and the keyboard there.

## What stays in the system preview

The sheet in the system preview (**Ctrl+Shift+Space**) is the same sheet,
with the same menus and annotations. What it lacks, it lacks because the
preview programs run no scripts: the search and the keyboard. And on Linux no
click there opens the reader. How the three previews otherwise differ is on
the [Platforms](platforms.qmd) page.
